solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sleeping partner may be in this close relationship

definitions.text: Sleeping partner may be in this close relationship

parts.note: the surface wants a silent investor in a business; the setter means someone literally asleep in bed
the surface wants intimacy between people; the setter means a garment worn close against the body

explanation.surface: A remark about an intimate partnership, with the sleeping partner of a business firm in view.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner is a business investor who stays silent; here it is literally someone asleep, wearing a garment in close contact with the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, worn in bed and close to the skin.

clue.text: Showing skill having no weak components?

definitions.meaning: a deft, tidy piece of work shows skill
a spirit served with no water or mixer has nothing to weaken it

explanation.walkthrough: A neat drink is served undiluted, with no water or mixer to weaken it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means deft, as in a neat piece of work, and undiluted, as in neat whisky.

clue.text: Looked for a second church seen in good light

parts.note: standard abbreviation for good

indicators.note: the church is seen inside the other letters

parts.note: to light on something is to land on it
Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone searches briefly for another church in a good light.
explanation.walkthrough: "Light" looks like illumination, but it is the verb meaning to settle or alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to look for only a moment.

clue.text: For these people, taking heroin is a fetish

parts.note: for them = to them
H is slang for heroin; it is removed

explanation.surface: A claim that for some group drug-taking has become an obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: "Taking heroin" suggests drug use, but here taking means removing: TO THEM loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish, in its old sense, is an object revered for its spirit, as a totem is.

clue.text: Faculty certainly entertained by people rowing

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight rowers
yes, certainly

explanation.surface: University staff are indeed wined and dined by the rowing club.
explanation.walkthrough: "Faculty" suggests university teachers; here it is a sense, one of the body's powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the faculties, the natural powers of the body.

clue.text: I'm surprised, not having left, that woman had cheated

indicators.note: the word goes without the letter

parts.note: WELL, an exclamation of surprise, minus one L
standard abbreviation for left; it is removed
she had = she'd

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to learn a woman who stayed had been unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: To welsh is to fail to pay a debt, especially a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a bet is to cheat by not paying up.

clue.text: Women's top that is least likely to fit?

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of women
Latin for that is, shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts for the women's top least likely to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The widest object is the one least likely to fit through a gap; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The widest thing is the hardest to squeeze through, so the least likely to fit.

clue.text: Parodied an old poem in a funny way

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: anagram of AN OLD POEM

explanation.surface: Someone made fun of an old poem.
explanation.walkthrough: "In a funny way" reads as part of the mockery, which suits the definition exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon is to mock through satire or parody.

clue.text: Special means of receiving stolen stock?

parts.note: stolen goods are hot
a line is a range of goods a shop stocks

explanation.surface: A question about how a fence takes in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests handling stolen goods, but a hotline is a dedicated phone line for receiving calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a special direct telephone line, a means of receiving calls.

clue.text: International cap making comeback gradually, with great effort

indicators.note: coming back means running the other way

parts.note: standard abbreviation for international
a cap on a jar is a lid
a gentle slope rises gradually

explanation.surface: A capped footballer slowly and painfully returns to the national side.
explanation.walkthrough: An international cap is the honour given to a player selected for their country; here it splits into I and LID.
explanation.definitionFit: To work diligently is to work hard and with care.

clue.text: Article on equality splitting support for divisive regime

indicators.note: the letters go into the middle of the support, splitting it

parts.note: aid is help or support

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: on a par means equal
the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on equality undermines backing for a divisive government.
explanation.walkthrough: "Article" wants to be a piece of writing; it is the grammatical article, and "on" in an across clue places it after the equality.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation, a regime built on division.

clue.text: Sound of bottle made from aluminium?

indicators.note: we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, which is mettle

explanation.surface: A question about the noise an aluminium bottle makes.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bottle" looks like a container; in British slang it means nerve, so losing your bottle is losing courage. The question mark marks aluminium as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: aluminium is one metal, so a thing made from it is metal, in the adjective sense.

clue.text: Granting authority to religious campaign during Advent

indicators.note: the campaign happens within the other word

parts.note: advent is an arrival or coming
a mission is a campaign to convert people

explanation.surface: A church is licensed to run a religious campaign in the weeks before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A pushes Advent towards the church season; here it is the plain word for arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: To commission someone is to give them authority to act or to take on a task.

clue.text: Eats early and extravagantly during holidays

indicators.note: the one word sits within the other

parts.note: holidays are breaks
to live fast is to live extravagantly

explanation.surface: Someone dines early and lavishly while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast here is the dissipated sense of fast living, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To breakfast is to eat the first meal, early in the day.

clue.text: Danger sign induced Conservatives to switch leaders

indicators.note: the two words swap their opening letters

parts.note: to lead is to induce; it takes the R from the next word
Conservatives are the political right; it takes the L from the word before

explanation.surface: A warning sign pushed the Tories into changing their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: "Switch leaders" is political in the surface; in the wordplay the leaders are the first letters of LED and RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light signals danger or tells traffic to stop.

clue.text: First person sister went out with could be in deep water

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
a nun is a religious sister
to date is to go out with

explanation.surface: Someone who dated a first sister might find themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: "In deep water" means in trouble in the surface, but here it is literal: covered by a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated means flooded, submerged in deep water.

clue.text: Trainee barrister's conclusion pretty much determined cases

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its last letter
the outer word holds the other like a case
nearly all the word, so drop the last letter

parts.note: INTENT, determined, minus its last letter
last letter of barrister

explanation.surface: A trainee lawyer's closing speech largely decided the court cases.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cases" looks like legal cases in this courtroom scene; it is a verb, meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a trainee working to gain experience.

clue.text: What crammer may do — help to get into Oxford?

definitions.note: the first definition is a verb, the second a noun
definitions.meaning: a crammer forces things into a tight space
an Oxford is a lace-up shoe, and the help is the curved tool that eases a foot in

explanation.surface: A tutor who crams students for exams helps them into Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is also a lace-up shoe, and a shoehorn helps you get your foot into it; to shoehorn is also to cram something in.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoehorn is to force into a tight space, as a crammer might; a shoehorn eases a foot into a shoe.

clue.text: An American transfixed by writer's hostility

indicators.note: pierced through, so the other letters run into it

parts.note: as written
abbreviation for the United States
the writer is I, and writer's is I'm

explanation.surface: An American reader is spellbound by an author's hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the writer or setter is often I, so writer's is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: animus, Latin for mind or spirit, came to mean a settled ill will.

clue.text: Route changed after during and before delivery

indicators.note: the letters of route are changed around
the new letters come after the other word

parts.note: in the war = during the war
anagram of ROUTE

explanation.surface: A delivery route was altered, with times given as during and before the drop.
explanation.walkthrough: "Delivery" suggests a parcel round alongside "route"; here it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero is Latin for in the womb, so before birth.

clue.text: Cast wicked character as her?

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin
wicked = evil

explanation.surface: A casting director puts an actress in a villain's role.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cast" is theatrical in the surface but here means threw off; the definition asks for a wicked character, female like her.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a malicious woman, a devilish character who is a her.

clue.text: Long-winded book, half of which is boring poetry

indicators.note: take half the letters of the word
the letters bore into the other word, going inside it

parts.note: verse is poetry
the first half of book

explanation.surface: A wordy book, half of which is dull poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boring" reads as dull; it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbose means using more words than needed, long-winded.

clue.text: Big Bang possibly boosted part of UK banking system

indicators.note: in a down clue, pushed up means read bottom to top

parts.note: Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom
giro is a British system of transferring money between bank accounts

explanation.surface: The 1986 Big Bang deregulation of the City gave a lift to part of British banking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Bang was also the name for the 1986 shake-up of London's financial markets, which fits the banking surface; here it is the birth of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the origin of the universe; possibly flags it as one example.

clue.text: One ultimately formed number involved in new organisation?

definitions.text: One ultimately formed number involved in new organisation?

parts.note: the surface wants a figure that finally took shape; the setter means one of the number of people who formed a body at the start
the surface wants any member of a new group; the setter means one who was there when it was founded

explanation.surface: A remark about someone among the founding group of a new body.
explanation.walkthrough: The members as a group ultimately formed the number of the organisation; each one who did so from the start is a founder member.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder member is one of the original members who set up an organisation.

clue.text: US author deleting line in book, subsequently?

indicators.note: deleting means striking something out of a text, as an editor deletes a letter

parts.note: Saul Bellow, American novelist
standard abbreviation for line; one L is removed

explanation.surface: An American writer cuts a line from a later book.
explanation.walkthrough: In a book, see below means see later in the text, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Below in a text refers to what comes subsequently.

clue.text: Given the circumstances, foundation has to let leader go

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a basis is a foundation; its B is removed

explanation.surface: In the circumstances, a charitable foundation must dismiss its head.
explanation.walkthrough: "Leader" suggests a boss being fired; it is the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: As is means in the present state, taking the circumstances as they are.

clue.text: Passed out

definitions.meaning: time that has passed has been used up
out as in worn out, exhausted or finished

explanation.walkthrough: Time spent is time passed; a spent force is finished, out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means passed, as time is, and used up or exhausted.

clue.text: Fairness of moral views

parts.note: moral = good
a look is a view

explanation.surface: A plea for justice rooted in ethical opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fairness" suggests justice beside "moral"; here it is the old sense of beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair once meant beautiful, so fairness is good looks.

clue.text: Did substitute put up with row after losing head?

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first
the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
DIN, a row or racket, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: A question whether a stand-in player tolerated a row after being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: "Row" rhymes with cow here: a noisy argument, so a din.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who stood in took another's place for a while, as a substitute does.

clue.text: Innovation of four distinct points separated by three more

indicators.note: the second group sits between letters of the first, splitting them

parts.note: the four compass points, north, east, west, south
three more compass points, north, east, south

explanation.surface: A new idea involving four points set apart by three further points.
explanation.walkthrough: The points are compass points, and all seven letters are N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Innovation names the quality as well as the new thing, and in that abstract sense it is the state of being new.
